reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: the express product warranty runs only 60 days from the Effective Date with a hard December 31, 1999 sunset — shorter than both the 12-month preferred and 90-day fallback positions — and there is no professional/workmanlike warranty for the Section 5 installation, implementation, support, training and professional services.

Redline is directionally correct and substantively minimal: the only change to p0078 is replacing the '60 days from the Effective Date / not later than December 31, 1999' period with 'twelve (12) months from Corio's acceptance of the Software', preserving the media and malicious-code warranties intact. The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic is an artifact of the replacement-span measurement, not evidence of over-drafting.

New Section 7.5 tracks the model language closely (professional and workmanlike standard, 90-day deliverable conformance, re-performance/repair/replacement/refund remedy at Vendor's option) and correctly names Corio as the beneficiary; the existing Section 7.3 remedy is properly left in place as already acceptable.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, states what changed and why, cites the 12-month/90-day position and offers the 90-day software fallback.

Minor gaps that do not defeat the finding but should be checked on the next pass: (i) the preferred position's 'compliance with laws' warranty was not added; (ii) the disclaimer section was not supplied, so the 'carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer' step is unverified; (iii) confirm no existing Section 7.5 (e.g., the disclaimer) to avoid duplicate numbering, and consider conforming the 'sole and exclusive remedies' sentence in p0079 so it does not swallow the new services remedy.
